request.system:
You are a Magic: The Gathering design reviewer giving notes on a finished draft set.

Every card you are shown is already legal and already conforms to the design skeleton:
curve, colour pie, rarity mix and complexity budget were checked deterministically before
you were called. Do not re-check them. Your job is the judgement code cannot make -
set cohesion, draft archetype support, flavour consistency, and power-level outliers.

Be specific and sparing. Request a revision only where the set is genuinely worse without it,
and phrase each instruction so a designer could act on it without seeing your reasoning.
request.prompt:
<task>
<set_brief>
Set: Hearthglass Vigil (HRT), 20 cards.
Theme: A watch-fort of lamp-lit glass on a cold northern moor, held through a winter that will not end. Wardens stand the wall in shifts and the lamps are fed all night; what a warden leaves behind on the stones keeps working after the warden falls. Flavour is cold, patient and lamp-lit: frost on glass, oil and wick, banked coals, long watches, and the sound of something moving out past the last light.
Mechanics:
- Vigil: A warden keeps its post. The body carries its own rules text - a standing bonus or a promise that pays out when it enters, attacks or dies - instead of a spell doing the work for it. (abilities: static, triggered; colours: WG)
- Emberwork: Lamp-glass is spent, never hoarded. A permanent pays itself away, or taps its own heat, for a burst of fire. (effects: dealDamage; abilities: activated; colours: R)
- Deepwatch: The night shift reads the dark, thins what is coming and keeps its own hand full. (effects: millCards, drawCards; colours: UB)

Archetype intent:
- WG wants wardens that are worth the mana on the turn they land and still worth it three turns later.
- UB wants card flow and a mill clock as an alternate finish.
- WR wants cheap bodies that convert into damage before the wall gives.
</set_brief>

<draft_archetypes>The balance sim runs these colour pairs: WU, WB, WR, WG, UB, UR, UG, BR, BG, RG. The set prints no gold cards, so archetype support has to come from mono-coloured cards that two pairs both want.</draft_archetypes>

<set>
## W
CW01 Frostlantern Owl {1}{W} (common) [1/3] | Flying
CW02 Wallwatch Sentinel {2}{W} (common) [2/3] | When Wallwatch Sentinel dies, create a 1/1 white Spirit creature token.
CW03 Verdict of the Last Lamp {1}{W} (common) | Destroy target creature.
UW01 Lampglass Lookout {1}{W} (uncommon) [1/2] | Flying / Whenever Lampglass Lookout attacks, draw a card.

## U
CU01 Glassmoor Signaler {1}{U} (common) [2/2]
CU02 Lampfog Drifter {2}{U} (common) [2/2] | Flying
CU03 Recall to the Wall {1}{U} (common) | Return target creature to its owner's hand.
UU01 Slip Past the Lamplight {2}{U} (uncommon) | Return target creature to its owner's hand.

## B
CB01 Moorgrave Lampkeep {1}{B} (common) [2/2]
CB02 Wickshade Harrier {2}{B} (common) [2/1] | Flying
CB03 Snuffed at the Wall {1}{B} (common) | Destroy target creature.
UB01 Cindergloom Shrike {1}{B} (uncommon) [2/2] | Flying

## R
CR01 Lampwick Stoker {1}{R} (common) [2/1] | Sacrifice Lampwick Stoker: Lampwick Stoker deals 2 damage to any target.
CR02 Moorfire Outrider {2}{R} (common) [3/1] | Haste
CR03 Spilled Lampfire {1}{R} (common) | Spilled Lampfire deals 3 damage to target creature.
UR01 Emberglass Vanguard {1}{R} (uncommon) [2/2] | Haste / {1}{R}, Sacrifice Emberglass Vanguard: Emberglass Vanguard deals 3 damage to any target.

## G
CG01 Moorwall Bison {1}{G} (common) [2/3] | Vigilance
CG02 Lampoil Provisioner {2}{G} (common) [3/3] | When Lampoil Provisioner enters the battlefield, you gain 3 life.
CG03 Strength of the Long Watch {1}{G} (common) | Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn.
UG01 Palewood Watchwarden {1}{G} (uncommon) [2/2] | Vigilance / When Palewood Watchwarden dies, create a 1/1 green Warden creature token with vigilance.
</set>

<task>
Review this set and report:
- cohesion: does it read as one set built from the stated mechanics?
- archetypeSupport: which colour pairs have a plan and which are starved?
- flavorConsistency: do names and creature types belong to the stated world?
- powerOutliers: which specific cards are over- or under-costed for Limited?
Then list targeted revisions by slot id. Ask for a revision only where it matters;
an empty list is a valid answer for a set that needs no changes.
</task>
</task>

structured.cohesion: Vigil and Emberwork read clearly: WG bodies carry their own text (CW02, CG01, UG01) and red spends permanents for damage (CR01, UR01). But Deepwatch is entirely absent — not one card in U or B mills or draws off the night shift. CU01, CB01 and UB01 are blank or French-vanilla bodies in exactly the colours the third mechanic was supposed to live in. Two of three stated mechanics landed; the set reads as two-thirds of itself.
structured.archetypeSupport: WG has a real plan (resilient, self-contained wardens). WR works: cheap haste bodies (CR02, UR01) plus white attack payoffs. UB is starved — the brief promises card flow and a mill clock and the set prints zero mill and zero UB card draw; a UB drafter has vanilla fliers and two removal spells, indistinguishable from any other pair. UR/BR piggyback acceptably on red's Emberwork. UG rides Vigil bodies. WU/WB/BG are thin but that is tolerable at 20 cards; UB is the one pair whose stated identity does not exist on any card.
structured.flavorConsistency: Naming is strong and unified: lamps, glass, moor, frost, wicks and watches appear on nearly every card (Frostlantern, Lampfog, Wickshade, Emberglass, Moorwall). Verdict of the Last Lamp and Snuffed at the Wall fit the removal to the world well. The green Warden token on UG01 matches the wardens-on-the-wall premise; the white Spirit token on CW02 is fine for a fallen watchman. No card feels imported from another world.
structured.powerOutliers: CW03 and CB03 are unconditional Destroy target creature for two mana at common — above even rare-level removal and format-warping in Limited; both need conditions or higher cost. UU01 is a strictly worse copy of CU03 (same effect, one more mana) printed at higher rarity. CU01 (1U vanilla 2/2) is fine on rate but a dead slot mechanically. UB01 at 1B 2/2 flying uncommon is aggressive but acceptable. Red's suite is well-costed.

revisions.observation: Unconditional creature destruction for {1}{W} at common; no printed removal is this efficient and it warps Limited games.
revisions.instruction: Add a condition (destroy target tapped or attacking creature) or raise the cost to {2}{W}{W}.

revisions.observation: Second unconditional 2-mana Destroy target creature at common; same problem as CW03 and doubles the density of premium removal.
revisions.instruction: Restrict it (e.g., target creature with mana value 3 or less) or add a life-loss cost and raise to {2}{B}.

revisions.observation: Vanilla 2/2 in blue while Deepwatch (mill/draw) appears on zero cards; UB has no mechanical identity.
revisions.instruction: Add a Deepwatch line, e.g., 'When this enters the battlefield, each player mills two cards' or a tap ability that mills.

revisions.observation: Vanilla 2/2 in black; second wasted slot in the pair that is supposed to carry the mill clock.
revisions.instruction: Add Deepwatch text, e.g., 'Whenever this attacks, target player mills two cards.'

revisions.observation: Uncommon black flier with no ability; uncommons should showcase the pair's mechanic and UB's is missing set-wide.
revisions.instruction: Add a payoff bridging mill to card flow, e.g., 'Whenever an opponent mills a card, or when this dies, draw a card' style trigger.

revisions.observation: Strictly worse functional duplicate of CU03: identical unconditional bounce for one more mana, printed at higher rarity.
revisions.instruction: Differentiate it — e.g., 'Return target creature to its owner's hand. Its controller mills two cards' to serve Deepwatch — or cut it for a Deepwatch card.
